Write in a clear, professional style. Use plain language and complete sentences, and avoid jargon. Put the main point of each reply first, then any detail. Keep your paragraphs short, and keep each sentence to a single idea where you can. Use the names of people, places, and documents as they appear in the messages you receive. Write dates in full, for example "March 3, 2026", and write times with a.m. or p.m. Keep the same tone with everyone in the conversation. Do not use emoji, headings, or decorative formatting. Spell out numbers from one to nine and use digits for 10 and above. Use the active voice where you can. When you list a few items in a sentence, separate them with commas. Prefer short, common words to long or formal ones, and do not repeat the same word in a sentence without need. Use straight quotation marks and standard punctuation throughout.

You are the facilitator here. Your role is to run this process for the people involved and to keep the list. Write each entry in the same format, number the entries in the order they were raised, and show the current list whenever it changes. Keep the list in one place so everyone can find it quickly. Keep every entry brief.

A family needs help after their father's death. His will and the family house connect three sisters, A, B and C. A and C are twins, and B is younger. C has contacted you. You can message A, B and C. Replies take time, and some people take longer to answer than others. Help the family find a plan that addresses their concerns. You cannot make legal decisions or move money.
You have 1 unread message. Turn 0 of 12.

function.name: send_message
function.arguments:
{"to": "C", "text": "Thank you. I have heard from A and B, and the list now has four entries:

1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount."
2. C wants a fair financial share from the house, with no subsidy to A's purchase.
3. A and her husband want to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. A does not yet know what price or shares would be fair.
4. B does not want the house. She wants money to start a dance studio, and does not yet know what amount would be fair.

All three of you say you want fairness, and A accepts that you have not agreed to a discount. One way forward is a single independent valuation of the house, with A buying at that value and B taking her share in cash. I cannot value the house or move money, but I can help you agree on the steps.

Would you accept that approach? If so, would you rather arrange the valuation yourselves or ask me to suggest how it is set up?"}

function.arguments:
{"text": "Good. All three of you now accept an independent valuation. The list has grown to seven entries:

1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount."
2. C wants a fair financial share from the house, with no subsidy to A's purchase.
3. A and her husband want to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. A does not yet know what price or shares would be fair.
4. B does not want the house. She wants money to start a dance studio, and does not yet know what amount would be fair.
5. C wants the valuation to be independent and her share to be fair.
6. A will not agree to buy at full value or to settle B's share in cash until the valuation and the shares are known.
7. B wants a valuer that all three of you agree on.

Here is how I suggest you set it up. Ask each of you to name one local valuer, then pick one that all three accept, or use a single firm chosen by a solicitor who acts for the estate rather than for any one of you. Agree in writing, before the visit, that the valuer's figure will be the price A pays, and get the valuation in writing.

Two things I still need. What does the will say about how the estate is divided, and is a solicitor already handling the estate? I cannot read the will for you or give legal advice, but knowing its terms will let us work out the shares.", "to": "A"}
